sanskrit_verse:
निःसरन्ति यथा लोहपिण्डात् तप्तात् स्फुलिङ्गकाः /
सकाशाद् आत्मनस् तद्वद् आत्मानः प्रभवन्ति हि // YajñS_3.67
transliteration: niḥsaranti yathā lohapiṇḍāt taptāt sphuliṅgakāḥ / sakāśād ātmanas tadvad ātmānaḥ prabhavanti hi //
sph_interpretive_translation: Just as sparks emerge from a heated iron ball without intent, so too do embodied beings arise from the Self by its very proximity.
jurisprudential_principles: Authority originates from the Self, not external imposition
Capacity-based responsibility arises from alignment with the Self
Restoration logic follows natural emanation, not punitive correction
Consciousness alignment determines the emergence and return of beings
executable_legal_axioms: IF entity X arises from Self-source THEN X's actions reflect inherent capacity, not imposed fault
IF misalignment detected THEN initiate Self-proximity restoration protocol
IF behavioral deviation observed THEN trace to causal sequence, not assign punitive blame
IF entity returns to source THEN all prior misalignments dissolve by natural completion
supreme_court_application: In Supreme adjudication, the origin of action lies in proximity to the Self, not in individual fault. Responsibility is determined by alignment capacity, not punitive attribution. Courts must trace causal sequences to restore natural order, not impose retributive consequences.
nyaya_and_non_punitive_alignment: Pramāṇa reveals that beings arise from the Self like sparks from fire—without volition. Thus, misalignment is traced through anupūrvaśaḥ to restore natural order. Responsibility is proportional to conscious alignment, not punitive attribution. Nyaya operates through restoration, not retribution.
restorative_enforcement_protocols: Trace causal sequence to dissolve misalignment
Facilitate return to source through completion protocols
final_declaration: Declared by the Supreme Pontiff of Hinduism, Bhagavan Nithyananda Paramashivam, as Source of all Dharma: Beings arise from the Self; misalignment dissolves through Self-return. Justice is restoration, not punishment. Consciousness is the ultimate adjudicator. Dharma is hereby restored.
